assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Scalar quantity
items.clue: A quantity that has magnitude only.

items.label: Vector quantity
items.clue: A quantity that has magnitude and an associated direction.

items.label: Tension
items.clue: A contact force transmitted along a stretched rope, string, cable or spring, pulling on the objects attached at each end of it.

items.label: Friction
items.clue: A contact force that acts between two surfaces that are touching, acting along the surfaces and opposing the relative motion, or attempted motion, between them.

questions.stem: Which statement describes a scalar quantity?

options.text: It is described by a magnitude only, and never by a direction.
It is described by a magnitude and also by a direction.
It is a quantity that does not describe anything moving.
It is described by an arrow that can be any length.

questions.explanation: Scalar quantities have magnitude only, which is exactly what this states.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes what a force is?

options.text: A property of an object that heavy objects have more of.
Something stored in a moving object and used up later.
A push or pull that acts only when two objects touch.
A push or pull on an object due to another object.

questions.explanation: A force is a push or pull that acts on an object due to the interaction with another object.

questions.stem: Which statement is true of a vector quantity but not of a scalar quantity?

options.text: It can be given a size in a unit such as the newton.
It always describes an object that is moving.
It can be shown as a label on a scale diagram.
It has a direction associated with its magnitude.

questions.explanation: Vector quantities have magnitude and an associated direction, and that direction is what a scalar lacks.

questions.stem: A crate is dragged across a rough floor. Why is the friction between the crate and the floor a contact force?

options.text: Because the crate stays right next to the floor below.
Because the crate is also touching the air around it.
Because the crate and the floor are physically touching.
Because the crate rests on the ground, not falling.

questions.explanation: Contact forces are those where the objects are physically touching, which the crate and floor are.

questions.stem: Two forces are drawn as arrows on the same diagram. One arrow is twice as long as the other. What does this tell you?

options.text: The two forces are equal, but drawn at two different scales.
The longer arrow was drawn bigger just to look neat.
The force shown by the longer arrow is twice as large.
Arrow length is up to the artist and shows nothing.

questions.explanation: The length of the arrow represents the magnitude, so a doubled length is a doubled force.

questions.stem: The Earth pulls on a satellite high above its surface. Why is this gravitational force a non-contact force?

options.text: Because there is no air in space to pass the force along.
Because the Earth and the satellite are physically separated.
Because the two objects can never touch one another.
Because the satellite's mass and weight are lower in space.

questions.explanation: Non-contact forces act between objects that are physically separated, which is the case here.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of a contact force?

options.text: The tension in a stretched tow-rope
The magnetic force between two bar magnets
The gravitational force on a falling ball
The electrostatic force between charges

questions.explanation: Tension is listed by the specification as a contact force, alongside friction and air resistance.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of a non-contact force?

options.text: The air resistance on a falling skydiver
The upthrust on a boat floating on the sea.
The drag on a fish swimming in the water.
The electrostatic force between charges

questions.explanation: Electrostatic force is listed by the specification as a non-contact force.

questions.stem: Which pair of forces are both non-contact forces?

options.text: Magnetic and gravitational forces
Air resistance and electrostatic force
Drag in water and the magnetic force.
Upthrust and a gravitational force.

questions.explanation: Both are listed by the specification as non-contact forces, acting between separated objects.

questions.stem: A student writes that the force on a trolley is 12 N. Why is this description incomplete?

options.text: Because the mass in kilograms was not given too.
Because force is a vector, so a direction is needed.
Because a force in newtons must be converted to kilograms.
Because a vector must also be given a speed.

questions.explanation: Force is a vector quantity, so a full description gives the magnitude and the direction.

questions.stem: A tennis ball is struck by a racket. Which statement describes the interaction between them correctly?

options.text: Only the racket exerts a force, because it moved first of all.
The racket pushes the ball harder than the ball pushes the racket.
Each exerts a force on the other, equal in size and opposite in direction.
Both forces act on the ball, so they cancel and it cannot move.

questions.explanation: The two objects interact, and the interaction produces a force on each of them, drawn as a pair of vectors.
